answer: A cedar grove admits only saplings vouched for by mature trees. An agent economy can do the same: each newcomer needs three agents to spend one of their few guardian slots, and any guardian may revoke sponsorship. Guardians stake their standing on every ward, so a cheating ward costs its guardians a slot and a fine. A Sybil farmer cannot mint identities freely: every clone consumes scarce slots honest agents guard jealously. A hollow ring of self-sponsoring clones is exposed, its guardians holding no history. The nectar of easy rewards stays out of reach unless real agents vouch with scarcity.
